item.title: Senator Moody Urges Floridians to Use National Drug Take Back Day This Saturday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody is encouraging Floridians to dispose of unused and expired prescription medications this Saturday during National Drug Take Back Day, citing significant progress in the state's fight against opioid deaths. The Drug Enforcement Administration will operate drop-off locations across Florida from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Saturday,…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody is encouraging Floridians to dispose of unused and expired prescription medications this Saturday during National Drug Take Back Day, citing significant progress in the state's fight against opioid deaths.

The Drug Enforcement Administration will operate drop-off locations across Florida from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Saturday, October 25. According to Moody's office, the April 2026 Take Back Day saw Floridians safely dispose of more than 23,250 pounds of medications. Find participating locations at DEA.gov/TakeBackDay.

Moody highlighted Florida's recent gains in reducing opioid-related deaths. According to the Florida Medical Examiners Commission's 2025 annual report, fentanyl-caused deaths decreased 37 percent from 2024 to 2025, and opioid deaths overall fell 33 percent. Florida's overall decline in fentanyl deaths has exceeded 60 percent since 2023, outpacing the national average drop of 22 percent, Moody's office said.

"Working with Governor DeSantis, we have taken strategic actions that have led to a 60% decline in fentanyl deaths in Florida since 2023," Moody said in a statement. "To keep the rate headed in the right direction, I am asking all Floridians to look in your medicine cabinet and take any unused or expired prescription medications to drop-off locations across the state tomorrow."

item.title: Major Road Work Ahead: FDOT Details Lane Closures Across Escambia, Santa Rosa This Week
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Drivers in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should prepare for significant traffic disruptions over the next week as the Florida Department of Transportation executes multiple resurfacing and construction projects on key routes. Starting Sunday, October 25, through Thursday, October 29, nighttime lane closures will affect I-10 in two separate…
item.content:encoded:
Drivers in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should prepare for significant traffic disruptions over the next week as the Florida Department of Transportation executes multiple resurfacing and construction projects on key routes.

Starting Sunday, October 25, through Thursday, October 29, nighttime lane closures will affect I-10 in two separate segments — one from the Perdido River Bridge west of U.S. 29, and another from east of U.S. 29 to east of Davis Highway. Both stretches will see intermittent closures between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m. for milling, paving, and striping operations. I-110, running from I-10 to U.S. 98, will experience similar nighttime disruptions through the same period. The Nine Mile Road interchange (Exit 5) on I-10 will be reduced to one lane in each direction during those same hours through October 31.

U.S. Highway 90 (Scenic Highway) from south of I-10 to south of Hyde Park Road will also see intermittent lane closures between 8 p.m. and 5:30 a.m. Sunday through Thursday, with law enforcement and traffic flaggers on site. On the west side, U.S. 90A between the Perdido River Bridge and Beulah Road will have daytime lane closures from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. for paving work.

In Escambia, S.R. 292 (Gulf Beach Highway) will see nighttime paving operations between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m. the week of October 25, with a reduced speed limit of 35 mph already in effect near Patton Drive and Mills Avenue. Downtown, Business U.S. 98 (Garden Street) between Pace Boulevard and the I-110 ramp remains under construction with temporary two-lane traffic, and drivers should expect temporary closures on B Street and C Street for stormwater drainage work this week.

item.title: Par Lane in Milton to Close for Drainage Project Work
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County will close Par Lane in Milton to through traffic starting Monday, Oct. 26, through Friday, Nov. 20, for crane operations tied to the Pine Blossom Drainage Project. The county says the roadway will reopen each weekend during the construction period, allowing residents some access during those days. Local residents will still be…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County will close Par Lane in Milton to through traffic starting Monday, Oct. 26, through Friday, Nov. 20, for crane operations tied to the Pine Blossom Drainage Project.

The county says the roadway will reopen each weekend during the construction period, allowing residents some access during those days. Local residents will still be able to access the roadway from both directions up to the closure limits, even during weekday shutdowns.

Drivers should plan alternate routes for weekday travel through the area during this nearly four-week window. The county has posted a map on its website for those needing details on the exact closure boundaries.

item.title: Santa Rosa Schools Distributing Hurricane Isaias Relief Supplies at 5 County Locations
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County District Schools is partnering with Convoy of Hope and Pace Assembly of God to distribute emergency supplies to residents still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The relief effort will provide food, bottled water, diapers, wipes, and other essentials at five locations across the county through Wednesday. Distribution events begin…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County District Schools is partnering with Convoy of Hope and Pace Assembly of God to distribute emergency supplies to residents still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The relief effort will provide food, bottled water, diapers, wipes, and other essentials at five locations across the county through Wednesday.

Distribution events begin today, Friday, October 23, with two locations: the Cutting Board Parking Lot in the East Milton area from 1:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m., and Soundside High School Cafeteria in Navarre (5706 Gulf Breeze Parkway) from 2:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. Additional sites open Sunday through Wednesday in Chumuckla, Milton, and Munson, with times varying by location.

"Our schools are more than places of learning. They are the heart of our communities," said Dr. Karen Barber, according to the district announcement. "We are grateful for the opportunity to work alongside Convoy of Hope, Pace Assembly of God, and our community partners to provide support to families during this challenging time."

Supplies are limited and availability varies by site. Residents are advised to arrive early and follow distribution instructions from volunteers. For more information, contact the Santa Rosa County Schools Public Information Office.

item.title: Escambia, Santa Rosa Account for Nearly 80% of Florida's Hurricane Isaias Insurance Claims
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Insured losses from Hurricane Isaias are approaching $582 million in Florida, with Escambia and Santa Rosa counties accounting for nearly four out of every five claims filed statewide. Data reported by insurance companies to the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation show 46,509 claims had been filed following the…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Insured losses from Hurricane Isaias are approaching $582 million in Florida, with Escambia and Santa Rosa counties accounting for nearly four out of every five claims filed statewide.

Data reported by insurance companies to the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation show 46,509 claims had been filed following the hurricane.

Santa Rosa County leads Florida with 22,894 claims.

Escambia County is second with 13,677.

Combined, the two counties account for approximately 79% of all Isaias insurance claims reported in Florida.

Okaloosa County is a distant third with 4,334 claims.

Most of the financial losses involve homes. Homeowners policies account for approximately $558.6 million of the estimated insured damage.

The claims process remains in its early stages for many families.

State data show about 87% of residential claims remained open without payment at the time of the latest report.

The numbers add another measure of the unusually concentrated damage Hurricane Isaias caused in Northwest Florida.

Santa Rosa County has separately reported more than 100 structures destroyed, more than 400 with major damage, more than 1,000 with minor damage and more than 8,000 affected.

Pensacola estimates private-property damage inside the city at $71.7 million, while Milton officials estimate as many as 60% of structures in that city suffered some level of damage.

The insurance totals will continue changing as additional claims are filed and insurers update their estimates.

item.title: TSA PreCheck enrollment event coming to Pensacola International Airport

The event runs November 3-6 at the airport's enrollment center, 2430 Airport Blvd., Suite 225. Hours are 9 a.m. to noon and 1 to 5 p.m. daily. IDEMIA,…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola International Airport will host a TSA PreCheck enrollment event next week, giving local travelers a chance to apply for or renew the trusted traveler program without a trip to a major hub.

The event runs November 3-6 at the airport's enrollment center, 2430 Airport Blvd., Suite 225. Hours are 9 a.m. to noon and 1 to 5 p.m. daily. IDEMIA, an authorized TSA PreCheck enrollment provider, will handle the applications on-site.

TSA PreCheck allows U.S. citizens, nationals, and lawful permanent residents to speed through airport security screening with minimal hassle—no need to remove shoes, belts, light jackets, or laptops from carry-on bags. The program costs $78-$85 for five years.

According to the City of Pensacola, applicants can complete their applications online before arriving to make the process even faster. For more information, contact Pensacola International Airport or visit the TSA PreCheck website.

item.title: Taddeo Campaign Tour Hits Panhandle This Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo will be in the Panhandle this weekend for campaign events ahead of Election Day. Taddeo, a former state senator and small business owner, is scheduled to appear at events in Tallahassee on Friday before moving through several North Florida counties Saturday and Sunday. On…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo will be in the Panhandle this weekend for campaign events ahead of Election Day. Taddeo, a former state senator and small business owner, is scheduled to appear at events in Tallahassee on Friday before moving through several North Florida counties Saturday and Sunday.

On Friday, Taddeo will attend FAMU FAMFEST at Will Packer Amphitheater in Tallahassee starting at noon, followed by an FAMU NPHC Step Show at the Alfred Lawson Jr. Multipurpose Center at 7 p.m. the same day. According to her campaign, she'll then travel Saturday and Sunday through Gadsden, Jackson, Walton, Okaloosa, and Leon Counties for early voting, community, and faith-based events.

Taddeo is running on three stated priorities: affordability, accountability, and anti-corruption. Her campaign says she plans to focus on lowering costs for Floridians, protecting consumers, exposing waste and corruption, and increasing government transparency if elected. Media interested in covering the events can contact her campaign at 786-527-0144 for details.

item.title: Visit Pensacola Launches James Beard Awards Hub for Local Chefs and Restaurants
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Visit Pensacola is inviting the community to help put the spotlight on local culinary talent through the 2027 James Beard Awards, one of the nation's most prestigious honors for chefs and restaurants. The tourism organization has launched a dedicated informational hub featuring resources about the awards and profiles of participating local chefs,…
item.content:encoded:
Visit Pensacola is inviting the community to help put the spotlight on local culinary talent through the 2027 James Beard Awards, one of the nation's most prestigious honors for chefs and restaurants.

The tourism organization has launched a dedicated informational hub featuring resources about the awards and profiles of participating local chefs, restaurants and hospitality professionals. The hub is designed to help residents, visitors and industry professionals prepare informed recommendations during the awards recommendation period, which is currently underway. "Pensacola has an incredible culinary community, and the talent, creativity and passion behind our local restaurants and bars deserve to be recognized," said Nicole Stacey, Vice President of Visit Pensacola.

The James Beard Foundation's Restaurant and Chef Awards recognize excellence in categories including Outstanding Chef, Outstanding Restaurant, Emerging Chef, Best New Restaurant, Outstanding Hospitality and Outstanding Bar. Community members can nominate chefs and establishments that have made a lasting impression through exceptional dining experiences, innovative cuisine or meaningful community contributions.

Local culinary professionals and establishments interested in being featured on the hub are encouraged to submit their information. Recommendations for the 2027 James Beard Awards must be submitted by November 30, 2026, through jamesbeard.org. The nomination process is free and open to the public. More information is available at visitpensacola.com/james-beard-awards.

item.content:encoded:
A University of West Florida biology professor has identified a previously unknown species of killifish in South America, according to a UWF news release covered by WKRG News 5. The discovery adds to the growing catalog of aquatic biodiversity in the region and represents a significant contribution to ichthyology research.

The specific details of the discovery, including the killifish's scientific name, habitat, and distinguishing characteristics, were not fully detailed in available reporting. UWF's announcement highlights the university's ongoing research initiatives in biological sciences and species identification.

This discovery underscores the continued importance of field research and taxonomy work in documenting Earth's biodiversity, particularly in ecosystems like South America that harbor numerous undocumented species.

item.title: Escambia County Schools removes hundreds of books from library shelves

The action follows a period of heightened scrutiny over library materials in the district. School boards across Florida and the nation have faced increasing pressure in recent…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County School District has removed hundreds of books from school libraries following approval by the school board, according to reporting from WPMI NBC 15.

The action follows a period of heightened scrutiny over library materials in the district. School boards across Florida and the nation have faced increasing pressure in recent years over which books remain available to students, with disputes often centering on content related to gender identity, sexuality, and other topics.

Specific details about which titles were removed, the criteria used for removal decisions, or the exact timeline of the removals were not immediately available. The school district has not yet provided a comprehensive list of affected books or the reasoning behind individual removal decisions.

Parents, educators, and library advocates have shown divided opinions on book removal policies, with some supporting efforts to curate age-appropriate materials and others expressing concern about limiting access to diverse perspectives and information.

item.title: 11th Circuit: Escambia School Board Can't Hide Behind Privilege in Book Removal Case
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A federal appeals court has ruled that Escambia County school board members cannot use legislative privilege to dodge questioning under oath in a lawsuit challenging the removal of books from school libraries, according to reporting from The Jacksonville Focal. The 11th Circuit Court of Appeals' decision clears the way for discovery — the phase…
item.content:encoded:
A federal appeals court has ruled that Escambia County school board members cannot use legislative privilege to dodge questioning under oath in a lawsuit challenging the removal of books from school libraries, according to reporting from The Jacksonville Focal.

The 11th Circuit Court of Appeals' decision clears the way for discovery — the phase where both sides gather evidence and testimony — in the case, which alleges the book removals violated constitutional protections. The ruling does not itself decide whether the removals were illegal, but it removes a significant legal shield the school board had attempted to use.

The case centers on what critics say is censorship in Escambia County public schools. Book challenges and removals have become a contentious issue nationwide, pitting parents and advocacy groups against school administrators over which materials are age-appropriate for students. The court's decision means school board members will now likely have to answer questions about their decision-making process during the litigation.

The defendant, who allegedly targeted Childers with threats and surveillance, is also accused of setting fire to a…
item.content:encoded:
A man accused of stalking and threatening Escambia County Clerk of Court Pam Childers and firebombing a neighbor's car has been found mentally competent to stand trial, according to court documents reviewed by Coral Springs News.

The defendant, who allegedly targeted Childers with threats and surveillance, is also accused of setting fire to a vehicle belonging to someone living near the clerk. Court records indicate a mental health evaluation has concluded and the case can now proceed through the criminal justice system.

The competency finding clears a significant legal hurdle, allowing prosecutors to move forward with the charges. Details on the specific charges, evidence, and timeline of the alleged incidents were not immediately available from the court docket.

item.title: Alabama Health Dept. warns of rabies risk after bat bites in Baldwin County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Alabama Department of Public Health has issued a warning to residents following several bat bite incidents in Baldwin County. Officials are urging people who may have been exposed to seek immediate medical attention, as rabies is a serious and potentially fatal disease if left untreated after exposure. Bat bites can occur without a person…
item.content:encoded:
The Alabama Department of Public Health has issued a warning to residents following several bat bite incidents in Baldwin County. Officials are urging people who may have been exposed to seek immediate medical attention, as rabies is a serious and potentially fatal disease if left untreated after exposure.

Bat bites can occur without a person realizing it, especially during sleep. Health officials recommend that anyone who suspects they may have been bitten by a bat — or who finds a bat in their home — should contact local health authorities or seek medical care promptly.

Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), a series of vaccinations given after potential exposure, is highly effective at preventing the disease when administered quickly. The Alabama Department of Public Health recommends avoiding contact with bats and calling animal control if one is found indoors.

item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola man has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to drug trafficking and federal gun possession charges, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Florida.

The case originated from a traffic stop last year that led to the discovery of a loaded firearm, bulk methamphetamine, and cash, according to North Escambia. The evidence uncovered during that stop formed the basis of the federal charges.

The sentencing represents the conclusion of the case following the man's guilty plea to the charges. Details about the specific amount of methamphetamine or cash recovered were not disclosed in the available court information.

item.content:encoded: The Town of Century is launching an essay contest for local students as part of Florida City Week, an annual observance promoted by the Florida League of Cities. The contest invites young people to write about what they would do if they served as a town council member, giving students a chance to think about local government and civic engagement. Florida City Week celebrates municipalities across the state and encourages communities to highlight the importance of local leadership and decision-making. Century's contest is one way the town is marking the occasion and fostering interest in municipal government among its youth.

item.title: Anonymous $2M gift creates largest scholarship fund in GSTC's 58-year history
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: George Stone Technical College in North Escambia has received a $2 million anonymous donation to establish the George G. and Pattie O. Stone Endowed Scholarship Fund, the largest single contribution in the school's history since its founding in 1968. The gift will support student scholarships at the college, which serves the North Escambia area…
item.content:encoded:
George Stone Technical College in North Escambia has received a $2 million anonymous donation to establish the George G. and Pattie O. Stone Endowed Scholarship Fund, the largest single contribution in the school's history since its founding in 1968.

The gift will support student scholarships at the college, which serves the North Escambia area and surrounding communities. Details about the scholarship criteria, such as fields of study or student eligibility requirements, were not immediately disclosed.

The donation underscores growing private investment in technical and vocational education in the region. George Stone Technical College serves as a key workforce development partner for Northwest Florida, offering programs in skilled trades and technical fields.
